subject: Japan edge activation — legal gating, SKU ask, and fallback lanes
messages:
From: Masato Kido <masato.kido@nanocloud.jp>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>; Yuki Sato <yuki.sato@nanocloud.jp>
Date: 2028-03-14 02:18:00 +0000
Subject: Pilot launch request - Tokyo edge + success criteria

Hiro / Redwood team,

Thanks for the time today. Summary from our side and what we need to lock to hit a May 1 pilot kickoff: 

- Pilot scope: 3-week closed beta for Tokyo Retail (40 stores) running recommendation and checkout assistant workloads.
- Traffic profile: peak is ~5M tokens/day, expected steady-state 1.2M tokens/day, bursts up to 10k TPS for short windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 60ms for generation requests.
- Data residency: all store PII must remain in Japan; encryption keys must be customer-managed (KMS).
- SLA ask: 99.9% availability for the pilot window.

Please confirm whether Redwood can provision a regional dedicated pool in Tokyo (ap-northeast-1 or nearby edge) with the above gating (KMS, audit logs). We are flexible on SKU mix if you can hit the latency and residency constraints.

Attached: nanocloud_pilot_requirements.pdf (high level).

Next step: can you send an initial SKU + capacity sketch and any compliance gating that would block a hosted-dedicated vs private deployment?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our program team needs to commit slots to store IT by 2028-03-20.

— Masato
CTO, Nanocloud
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: masato.kido@nanocloud.jp, procurement@tokyo-retail.co.jp
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-14 09:46:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Pilot launch request - initial capacity sketch and gating

Masato / Yuki — thanks, and great to see the clear success criteria. High-level response below; ops/legal will confirm the gating items.

1) Can hit latency/residency with two options:
   - Hosted Dedicated in Tokyo edge (preferred): 3x H100-80GB equivalents (in an HV-optimized rack) for burst safety, plus 2x L4s for low-cost embedding/recall. This targets p95 ~45–55ms on your request profile with continuous batching.
   - Private VPC (customer-managed): If KMS/HSM tenancy is non-negotiable, we can deliver a private deployment on your infra with the same SKU profile but with additional lead time (~6–8 weeks).

2) Initial SKU / capacity sketch (ballpark monthly burn):
   - 3x H100-80GB (inference) — reserved for peak 2.5k concurrent decoding capacity; modeled tokens/day: ~5–6M.
   - 2x L4 (edge embedding/cache) — handles lightweight calls and caching; reduces token compute cost by ~18% in our sim.
   - Prefetch KV cache and a 1.2 TB warm SSD for low-latency stateful sessions.
   Estimated committed monthly cost (hosted-dedicated): ~$165k/month (includes reserved GPU and network egress estimate).

3) Fallback lanes: we propose an EU fallback (Frankfurt) and a US fallback (us-west-2) for capacity fallback in case of local issues. Fallback will degrade latency predictably; we'll provide per-route SLOs.

4) Gating items for legal/compliance: Irene, can you confirm if the KMS customer key requirement++audit logs & proof-of-control can be satisfied in hosted-dedicated? Also flag whether SOC2 + ISO attestation is sufficient or if they need dedicated on-prem keys.

5) Ops ask: Vanessa, can you provision a short capacity sketch and a booking ask we can show Nanocloud today? We need to know lead-times for H100 reservations and whether a temporary burst to Seoul (to reduce lead time) is feasible.

Action items:
- Vanessa: ops capacity sketch + earliest reservation windows (V)
- Irene: legal/compliance gating list + whether hosted-dedicated can satisfy KMS/HSM (I)
- Hiro: will produce a one-page SOW + provisional cost table and a Drive folder with runbook links.

I attached a proposed SKU workbook (hiro-proposed-sku-mix.xlsx) with the above numbers.

Regards,
Hiro Tanaka
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
Cc: Masato Kido <masato.kido@nanocloud.jp>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15 07:22:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Pilot launch request - compliance gating and options

Hiro / team / Masato — quick legal/compliance note after reviewing the requirement doc and our hosted-dedicated capabilities: 

- KMS: Hosted-dedicated supports CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via our integrated KMS connectors, but we do not offer customer HSM appliances in the shared-hosted model. If Nanocloud requires HSM-backed keys under their direct control, we must move to a Private deployment (customer-managed HSM) or support a co-managed model (longer timeline).
- Data residency: We can cryptographically ensure encrypted-at-rest in Tokyo region and enforce routing policies. However, logs containing telemetry metadata (synthesized traces) may transit control plane services in our control plane; for strictly zero-control-plane-data residency, Private deployment is required.
- Audit evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, and per-customer audit logs for the hosted-dedicated pool. For in-person/evidence-level audits requiring on-prem evidence, Private will be needed.
- Contract redlines: procurement clause to add for Nanocloud: explicit data residency SLA, KMS responsibilities, and a fallback failover policy. I will prepare minimal contract language for the SOW.

Drive checklist (public to participants): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNanocloudPilot — contains: onboarding checklist, SOC2 extract, CMEK integration guide.

If Masato can confirm whether HSM is mandatory vs CMEK, we can quickly determine path: Hosted-dedicated (2–3 weeks for reservation + config) vs Private (6–8 weeks + tighter presales).

— Irene
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Masato Kido <masato.kido@nanocloud.jp>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-17 16:42:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Pilot launch request - ops booking ask and timeline

Masato / Hiro — ops capacity plan and timeline below. I included conservative lead-times and an alternative to reduce lead time by mixing region burst capacity.

Plan A (Hosted-dedicated in Tokyo):
- Reserve 3x H100-80GB equivalent nodes + 2x L4 nodes. Lead time: 10 business days to reserve and run the initial onboarding (includes config and CMEK wiring).
- Warm-up window: 3 days.
- Estimated monthly reserved commit: 12,000 GPU-hours equivalent (we'll map to our internal SKU).
- Ops runbook: ops-japan-capacity-plan.csv attached (contains per-day token mapping, expected p95 latency curves, and scaling triggers).

Plan B (Hybrid fast-start):
- Reserve 2x H100 in Seoul (quicker availability) for burst lanes and 1x H100 in Tokyo. Use routing to prefer Tokyo; burst to Seoul during peaks. Lead time: 3–5 business days for the Seoul reservation, additional 7–10 for Tokyo full coverage.
- This reduces up-front reserved cost but yields slightly higher p95 during bursts (~80–100ms).

Costs (rough):
- Plan A: ~$165k/month (matches Hiro sketch).
- Plan B: ~$125k/month initially while Tokyo reservation completes; expected to normalize to Plan A pricing after full provisioning.

Action items for Nanocloud:
1) Confirm HSM mandatory vs CMEK (key gating) — if CMEK OK, we can proceed with Plan A and meet May 1.
2) Sign SOW (Irene will push minimal clauses) or approve a temporary pilot addendum for Plan B.
3) Approve target commit and we will issue a booking window (non-binding hold) to reserve H100 capacity.

If you want, we can do a short call tomorrow to walk through the ops CSV and failover behavior.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Capacity & Region Ops, Redwood Inference
(attachment: ops-japan-capacity-plan.csv)
